solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slowly moving — stealing — quietly away

indicators.note: away tells us the quiet letter goes off, leaving the rest of the word behind

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone creeps off softly while thieving.
explanation.definitionFit: Inching along is creeping forward a tiny distance at a time, so it is moving slowly.

clue.text: Nine ladies dancing somewhere on the motorway?

indicators.note: dancing says the letters move about into a new order, like the carol's nine ladies

explanation.surface: The carol's nine ladies dancing turn up on a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The inside lane is the left-hand lane of a British motorway, a place on the road.

clue.text: Scenic country farm near Dolgellau, last of all — found here

definitions.text: Scenic country farm near Dolgellau, last of all — found here

indicators.note: last of all takes the final letter of every one of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A pretty rural farm close to Dolgellau is located here.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolgellau is a town in north Wales, so the whole clue also points to the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymru is the Welsh name for Wales, the land where Dolgellau and its scenic farms lie.

clue.text: Without a will in the States, husband and son must leave

indicators.note: must leave says these letters are taken out of the phrase

explanation.surface: An American dies with no will, and the man of the house and his boy have to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H and the last S from INTHESTATES leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying intestate means dying with no valid will in place.

clue.text: Awkward, if essential part of Oberammergau, cherished

indicators.note: essential part of says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something is awkward though central to a cherished Bavarian village.
explanation.walkthrough: Oberammergau is a Bavarian village famous for its Passion Play; the letters straddle the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche means socially clumsy or lacking grace, so awkward.

clue.text: Initially, geese are laying specially for lasses

indicators.note: Initially says to take the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Geese laying eggs for the benefit of some young women: a nod to the six geese a-laying of the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Gals is an informal word for girls or young women, the same as lasses.

clue.text: Hair application allergy not oddly brought up

indicators.note: brought up, in a down clue, says the kept letters read from bottom to top
not oddly says skip the odd-placed letters and keep the even ones

explanation.surface: A hair product triggered an allergic reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of allergy give LEG, which 'brought up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gel is a jelly-like styling product applied to hair.

clue.text: Fibs about United v Villa initially affected players?

indicators.note: about says the fibs go round the other letters

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names
v is the short form of versus, a single letter V

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of Villa

explanation.surface: Lies about a football match between United and Aston Villa upset the players.
explanation.definitionFit: Luvvies is British slang for theatrical actors, mocked as gushing and affected.

clue.text: Boy perhaps, embraced by maids a-milking

indicators.note: embraced by says the letters sit held inside the words maids a-milking

explanation.surface: A lad is hugged by the eight maids a-milking of the Christmas carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam is a boy's name, so a boy is one example of someone so called; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: One arranging turtle dove (not first or seventh)?

indicators.note: arranging says the remaining letters are put into a new order
not first or seventh drops the letters in positions one and seven of the phrase turtle dove

explanation.surface: Someone sets out the two turtle doves of the carol, the gift sent by 'my true love'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not first or seventh' strips T and D from TURTLEDOVE, leaving URTLEOVE; 'arranging' shuffles that.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Twelve Days of Christmas the giver of every gift is 'my true love', the one person doing the sending.

clue.text: Alibi let us off, being of some value

indicators.note: off says the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An alibi gets us off the hook, which makes it worth something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something utilisable can be put to use, so it has some practical worth.

clue.text: Detective sergeant collecting unusual percussion instruments

indicators.note: collecting says the sergeant's letters gather up the other word inside them

parts.note: DS is the police abbreviation for detective sergeant
rum is old British slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A police officer gathers some odd items for the band, perhaps the twelve drummers drumming.
explanation.definitionFit: Drums are struck instruments, the core of the percussion section.

clue.text: Old Jute settler, English in his time

indicators.note: in places the English abbreviation inside the other letters

explanation.surface: An early settler was English for his day.
explanation.definitionFit: Hengist was a legendary fifth-century Jutish leader who, with Horsa, came to Kent; so an early Jute who settled in Britain.

clue.text: Song's nine unusually bright red flashy features?

indicators.note: unusually says the letters come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A carol's nine verses are strangely full of showy colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Neon gives a red glow, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon-filled tubes glow bright red, so illuminated signs flash on shopfronts.

clue.text: Secular fella, I calculate, in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man of the world, someone who calculates, is described as worldly.
explanation.definitionFit: Laical relates to the laity, people outside the clergy, hence non-religious or secular.

clue.text: Is hot? No, perishing, truthfully

indicators.note: perishing says the letters break up and are reformed

explanation.surface: Is it hot? No, honestly it's freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perishing' reads as freezing cold, answering the question, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: In sooth is an archaic phrase meaning in truth or indeed.

clue.text: A lord's leaping around at the back

indicators.note: leaping around says the letters jump about into a new order, like the carol's ten lords a-leaping

explanation.surface: One of the ten lords a-leaping capers about the back of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorsal describes the back of an animal, as with a fish's dorsal fin on its upper side.

clue.text: Headless bugler grabbing one: what could be more hideous?

indicators.note: grabbing says what is left takes hold of the other letter inside it
Headless says the word bugler loses its first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A beheaded bugler clutches something: what could be uglier?
explanation.walkthrough: Headless bugler is UGLER, which takes I.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of ugly; something uglier is more unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Money saved, an inducement to a calling bird?

definitions.meaning: a sum put aside for the future, kept against later needs

definitions.text: an inducement to a calling bird?
definitions.meaning: a fake egg left in a nest to coax a hen to lay there; the calling bird is the carol's day-four gift

explanation.surface: A savings pot doubles as a lure for one of the four calling birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Savings put by are a 'nest egg'; literally a dummy egg is placed in a nest to encourage a bird to lay.

clue.text: Steamship going around pale swimmers

indicators.note: going around says the ship's letters encircle the other word

explanation.surface: A steamer passes some pallid birds on the water, the seven swans a-swimming of the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Swans are water birds that glide on lakes, so swimmers in the carol's phrase.

clue.text: First half of gift on day one is separate

indicators.note: First half of takes the opening portion of the gift's name

parts.note: on the first day of Christmas the carol sends a partridge in a pear tree

explanation.surface: Half of the first day's present is a thing apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means separated or set aside from others, so separate.

clue.text: Novelist William accepting right gift for day five

indicators.note: accepting says the novelist's name takes in the other letter

parts.note: William Golding wrote Lord of the Flies

explanation.surface: A writer receives the carol's fifth-day present.
explanation.definitionFit: On the fifth day of Christmas the carol's giver sends five gold rings, so one is that day's gift.

clue.text: Point to daughter, getting up

indicators.note: getting up, in a down clue, says the letters read upwards

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter; that the letters also run backwards through the printed words is a coincidence of the charade, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: Someone directs attention to their daughter as she rises.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a small point or mark, such as a full stop.

clue.text: A pound for a priest's vestment

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A cleric's robe costs a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: An alb is the long white linen robe worn by a priest at Mass.

clue.text: Gunned down last of pipers piping

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word pipers

explanation.surface: The carol's eleven pipers piping are mown down.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot is the past participle of shoot, so someone shot has been gunned down.

clue.text: Got up to collect set award?

indicators.note: to collect says the outer word gathers the other inside it

parts.note: to get up a subject is to learn it, as done by rote

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to receive a prize for the film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up' looks like ROSE, which starts the answer, but the parse is ROTE holding SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge given as a prize, as at a horse or flower show.
